title: unknown vs any
description: Learn the difference between unknown and any, and when to use each in TypeScript and React applications.

data.text: TypeScript gives you two ways to opt out of strict typing: `any` and `unknown`. They sound similar, but they behave very differently. Understanding the difference is one of the easiest ways to make your React applications more reliable.

When you mark something as `any`, you are telling TypeScript to step back and stop checking anything related to that value. You can call any method, pass it anywhere, and assign it to any variable without a single warning. In a small script this is harmless, but in a React app it can silently break your UI.

data.title: The Danger of any
data.content: Using any disables type checking entirely

data.text: `unknown` also accepts any value, but it does not let you use that value until you prove its type first. If you try to call a method on an `unknown` value, TypeScript will stop you until you narrow the type with a check such as `typeof`, an array guard, or a custom validator.

data.title: Narrowing unknown Safely
data.content: unknown forces you to validate before use

cards.title: any
cards.description: Opts out of type checking completely. The compiler trusts you blindly.
pros: Quick way to silence errors during migration
Useful with loosely typed third-party libraries
cons: Can spread through the codebase like a virus

cards.title: unknown
cards.description: Accepts any value, but requires type checking before you use it.
pros: Forces you to handle unexpected shapes
cons: Requires runtime checks when the shape is unknown

data.text: React developers often reach for `any` when handling API responses, form inputs, or event handlers. Switching to `unknown` can catch errors before they reach the user.

data.title: Form Input Handling
Prefer unknown Over any
data.text: Use `any` only as a last resort, such as when migrating a large untyped codebase. For new code, `unknown` keeps the compiler honest and prevents invalid state from spreading through your components.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: `any` disables all type checking and lets bugs hide until runtime
`unknown` accepts any value but requires validation before use
Use `unknown` for API responses, external data, and user input
data.takeaway: unknown gives you the flexibility of any while keeping the safety net of TypeScript.
